title: Gratuitous Clone-on-Write (The Paranoid Allocator)
pattern: Cloning or deeply duplicating immutable internal data on every access, when returning a borrowed reference is structurally safe and sufficient.
why_bad: It incurs high, unnecessary CPU and memory allocation overhead. This defeats the explicit safety guarantees of a modern borrow checker, replacing structured ownership with defensive duplication theater.
detection: The presence of `.clone()` or `.to_owned()` on internal, read-only structures in getter/accessor implementations returning to consumers within the same thread.
fix: Return a borrowed reference (`&T` or `&str`) instead of a full clone, delegating lifecycle and access safety to the compiler.
source: Robert C. Martin, *Clean Code*, Chapter 17, G5 ("Duplication") / "Corollary: Use Copies of Data" / Steve McConnell, *Code Complete*, Section 8.8.
